title: Hono Netlify Adapter not working out of the box + Solution
body:
### What version of Hono are you using?

4.3.11

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

Netlify

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

When using the `npm create hono@latest` command to create an app for deployment to Netlify, the app doesn’t build properly.

Running `netlify dev` results in a series of errors:
```
◈ Failed to run Edge Function index:
TypeError: Import 'https://registry-staging.deno.com/@hono/hono/meta.json' failed: error sending request for url (https://registry-staging.deno.com/@hono/hono/meta.json): error trying to connect: dns error: failed to lookup address information: nodename nor servname provided, or not known
    at file:///Users/peter/Documents/explorations/hononetlify/netlify/edge-functions/index.ts:1:22
    at async file:///Users/peter/Documents/explorations/hononetlify/.netlify/edge-functions-serve/dev.js:7:35 {
  code: "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND"
}
TypeError: Import 'https://registry-staging.deno.com/@hono/hono/meta.json' failed: error sending request for url (https://registry-staging.deno.com/@hono/hono/meta.json): error trying to connect: dns error: failed to lookup address information: nodename nor servname provided, or not known
    at file:///Users/peter/Documents/explorations/hononetlify/netlify/edge-functions/index.ts:1:22
    at async file:///Users/peter/.nvm/versions/node/v22.4.1/lib/node_modules/netlify-cli/node_modules/@netlify/edge-bundler/deno/config.ts:12:10 {
  code: "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND"
}
```

## Solution (what worked for me)
Use the URL method of importing packages instead of jsr.

Replace the
```ts
import { Hono } from 'jsr:@hono/hono'
import { handle } from 'jsr:@hono/hono/netlify'
```

with
```
import { Hono } from "https://deno.land/x/hono@v4.3.11/mod.ts";
import { handle } from "https://deno.land/x/hono@v4.3.11/adapter/netlify/index.ts";
```

Or with
```
import { Hono } from "https://esm.sh/jsr/@hono/hono@4";
import { handle } from "https://esm.sh/jsr/@hono/hono/netlify";
```


Hope this helps

### What is the expected behavior?

```
◈ Static server listening to 3999

   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │                                                 │
   │   ◈ Server now ready on http://localhost:8888   │
   │                                                 │
   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

◈ Loaded edge function index
```

### What do you see instead?

```
◈ Failed to run Edge Function index:
TypeError: Import 'https://registry-staging.deno.com/@hono/hono/meta.json' failed: error sending request for url (https://registry-staging.deno.com/@hono/hono/meta.json): error trying to connect: dns error: failed to lookup address information: nodename nor servname provided, or not known
    at file:///Users/peter/Documents/explorations/hononetlify/netlify/edge-functions/index.ts:1:22
    at async file:///Users/peter/Documents/explorations/hononetlify/.netlify/edge-functions-serve/dev.js:7:35 {
  code: "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND"
}
TypeError: Import 'https://registry-staging.deno.com/@hono/hono/meta.json' failed: error sending request for url (https://registry-staging.deno.com/@hono/hono/meta.json): error trying to connect: dns error: failed to lookup address information: nodename nor servname provided, or not known
    at file:///Users/peter/Documents/explorations/hononetlify/netlify/edge-functions/index.ts:1:22
    at async file:///Users/peter/.nvm/versions/node/v22.4.1/lib/node_modules/netlify-cli/node_modules/@netlify/edge-bundler/deno/config.ts:12:10 {
  code: "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND"
}
```

### Additional information

I solved my issue by using one of the url importing methods `https://deno.land/x/hono`, there are others like esm `https://esm.sh/jsr/@hono/hono@4`, and perhaps the create command + example could show one of them.
Appreciate this is specific to deploying on Netlify, but that's what the create template using Netlify suggest user would be able to do.

title: Don't require `return` to send responses
body:
### What is the feature you are proposing?

In Go, for example, one can do:
```go
c.JSON(http.StatusOK, /* ... */)
// do something else afterwards...
return
```
And that allows one to send a response without having to terminate execution.

Ideally, this would be allowed in Hono. Currently, you need to 
```typescript
return c.json({ /* ... */ })
// can't do something afterwards
```

In the same line, Vercel already added two functions to address this need:
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/after
- https://vercel.com/docs/edge-middleware/middleware-api#waituntil

title: Request for Guidance: Application Structure & Best Practices for Enterprise Applications
body:
### What is the feature you are proposing?

## Overview

As a developer building enterprise applications with Hono.js, I've had to make many architectural decisions to maintain separation of concerns, dependency injection, validation, and documentation. While Hono's unopinionated nature is valuable, some guidance on recommended patterns would be extremely helpful to reduce cognitive overhead and establish conventions.

## Current Structure

I've implemented the following structure for a medium-to-large application using Hono:

```
/src
├── core/                      # Core application components
│   ├── db/                    # Database schema and migrations
│   ├── errors/                # Error handling system
│   ├── factories/             # Creation factories
│   ├── logging/               # Logging utilities
│   └── monitoring/            # Monitoring and observability
│
├── features/                  # Feature modules
│   ├── auth/                  # Authentication feature
│   ...
│   └── users/                 # User management
│       ├── me/                # User profile management
│       ├── media/             # Media handling
│       └── notifications/     # User notifications
│
├── integrations/              # Third-party service integrations
│   ├── assets/                # Asset management
│   ├── cache/                 # Caching system
│   ├── database/              # Database connection
│   ├── email/                 # Email services
│   ├── firebase/              # Firebase integration
│   └── phone-verification/    # Phone verification services
│
├── shared/                    # Shared utilities and components
│   ├── middlewares/           # Application middlewares
│   ├── services/              # Shared services
│   └── utils/                 # Utility functions
│
├── app.ts                     # Main application setup
├── container.ts               # DI container setup
├── index.ts                   # Application entry point
└── openapi.ts                 # OpenAPI integration
```

Each feature module follows this pattern:

```
/feature
├── api/                 # HTTP endpoints
├── di.ts                # Dependency injection registration
├── docs/                # Documentation
│   ├── diagrams/        # Flow diagrams
│   ├── notes/           # Implementation notes
│   └── openapi/         # OpenAPI specification
├── index.ts             # Feature exports
├── repositories/        # Data access
├── services/            # Business logic
│   ├── domain/          # Core business logic
│   └── infrastructure/  # Technical services
├── types/               # Type definitions
├── use-cases/           # Application use cases
└── validation/          # Input validation
```

## Pain Points

1. **Dependency Injection**: Since Hono doesn't have built-in DI, I'm using Awilix, which creates additional boilerplate code in each feature module.

2. **Validation/DTOs**: There's no standardized approach for input validation, resulting in custom solutions and additional cognitive overhead.

3. **API Documentation**: Creating and maintaining OpenAPI docs manually is time-consuming.

4. **Code Organization**: The current structure follows a clean architecture approach but results in many files and directories, creating a high cognitive load when working with the codebase.

5. **Use-Case Pattern**: I've implemented a use-case pattern to coordinate services and prevent circular dependencies (1 API <> 1 USE CASE <> N SERVICES <> N REPOSITORIES), but I'm unsure if this is the right approach.

## Questions

1. Is there a recommended application structure for larger Hono.js applications that balances separation of concerns with developer experience?

2. What are the best practices for organizing code in a Hono.js application to avoid the "boilerplate trap"?

3. Are there any recommended libraries or patterns for handling common concerns like validation, DI, and API documentation that work well with Hono?

4. Would a more file-based routing approach (like Next.js) with colocation of logic be more appropriate for Hono applications?

5. Could the Hono documentation include examples of different application structures based on application size and complexity?

## Community Feedback

Several developers have expressed similar concerns on various platforms. The consensus seems to be that while Hono's unopinionated nature is valuable, some guidance on recommended patterns would help developers make better architectural decisions and avoid reinventing the wheel.

## Potential Solutions

1. **Official Structure Templates**: Provide example structures for different sizes of applications (small, medium, large).

2. **Best Practices Guide**: Document recommended approaches for common concerns like validation, DI, and API documentation.

3. **Starter Kits**: Create official starter kits or templates that implement proven patterns.

4. **Community Showcase**: Feature community projects that demonstrate effective structures for various use cases.

Thank you for considering this request. Hono is a fantastic framework, and some guidance on these points would make it even more accessible for complex applications.

title: Support for Bun + Socket.io + Hono Integration (Works on Node.js, not Bun)
body:
### What is the feature you are proposing?

### Describe the feature request
I’d like to request support (or guidance) for integrating **Socket.io** with **Hono** when running on **Bun**. Currently, using Socket.io with Hono works seamlessly on Node.js, but the same approach does not function as expected on Bun.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Yes. When trying to use Socket.io with Hono on Bun, the server either fails to start, or WebSocket connections do not establish properly. This is a blocker for projects that want to use the performance of Bun with real-time features provided by Socket.io and the simplicity of Hono.

### Describe the solution you’d like
-  An example of integrating Socket.io with Hono on Bun and/or If there are technical blockers in Bun or Hono, a roadmap or explanation would be helpful
-  Using other WebSocket libraries, but Socket.io is preferred for its features and ecosystem

### Additional context

Node.js: Works fine with Socket.io and Hono  
Bun: Fails to integrate with Socket.io and Hono

title: 'Vary' response header is overwritten when using CORS middleware unless provided in request headers
body:
### What version of Hono are you using?

4.10.1

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

Cloudflare Workers (locally with `wrangler dev`, 4.43.0)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Hi. I'm using the `hono/cors` middleware and also setting the `Vary` header to `Accept` for responses in my controller. I noticed that the actual server response is `Vary: Origin` instead.

After checking the source code I see that Hono checks the request vary header, and if that is not there, it will overwrite it on the response. Does it make sense that it should check the response vary header instead? New to the whole vary header, so I'm assuming it is not normal practice for a request from the client to include it. Or is there a reason for this, i.e. security?

https://github.com/honojs/hono/blob/4b796cfb0b105418bbf806050e788741f2739125/src/middleware/cors/index.ts#L112

### Reproduction

I've created a minimal reproduction repository: https://github.com/Juuldamen/hono-vary-cors-issue. See the readme for test commands.

1. Run server that has a CORS middleware and a controller that returns a response with the `Vary` header that has a value different than `Origin`.
2. Send a HTTP request, for minimal repro: `curl -i http://localhost:8787/test`

### What is the expected behavior?

The `Vary` header value on the HTTP response should include the values as set on the response in the controller. Preferably it should check if the value includes `Origin` and if not add it when the CORS middleware is used. To prevent issues with CORS if the developer forgets to add this to their `Vary` response value.

### What do you see instead?

The `Vary` header value in the response only includes `Origin`. Unless the request includes the `Vary` header itself. Than the response will include the same `Vary` value as the request.

### Additional information

As briefly discussed on Discord: https://discord.com/channels/1011308539819597844/1012485912409690122/1427417950037606421

RPC Client types are too tightly coupled to native fetch API, making custom fetch clients impractical
body:
## Description

The RPC client accepts a custom `fetch` implementation via options, but the `ClientResponse` types are tightly coupled to the native fetch API. This makes it impractical to use popular fetch wrappers like `ofetch`, `ky`, or `axios` without significant type workarounds.

## Current Behavior

When using a custom fetch client, the `ClientResponse` types still expect native fetch methods like `res.ok`, `res.json()`, `res.text()`, etc. However, custom fetch clients have different APIs and behaviors:

- **ofetch**: Throws errors on non-2xx responses instead of returning a response object with `ok: false`
- **ky**: Similar behavior with a different API surface
- **axios**: Uses `data` property instead of methods like `.json()`

## Example

Here's a real-world case using `ofetch` in a Nuxt application:

```typescript
import { createClient } from '@sdk/v1'
import type { ClientResponse } from 'hono/client'

export default function useApi() {
  const client = createClient('', {
    fetch: useAuthFetch(), // ofetch-based custom fetcher
  })

  return client
}

// Workaround: Type utility to extract 200 response since ofetch throws on non-2xx
export function res200<T>(
  res: T,
): Extract<T, { status: 200 }> extends ClientResponse<infer Body, 200, any>
  ? Body
  : Extract<T, { status: 200 }> {
  return res as any
}

// Usage - must use .then(res200) after every RPC call
const result = await client.v1.orders.$get({ query: q }).then(res200)
```

The custom fetch implementation:

```typescript
export function useAuthFetch() {
  const instance = $fetch.create({ // ofetch
    baseURL: '/api',
    
    onRequest({ options }) {
      // Add auth headers
    },
    
    async onResponseError({ response }) {
      // Handle 401, refresh tokens, etc.
      // ofetch throws here for non-2xx responses
    },
  })

  return instance
}
```

## Problem

1. The `ClientResponse` type assumes native fetch behavior
2. Custom fetch clients have different APIs and error handling strategies
3. TypeScript doesn't know that non-2xx responses will never arrive as normal response objects when using `ofetch`
4. Users must create type workarounds like `res200()` for every RPC call
5. This defeats the purpose of having type-safe RPC calls

## Impact

- Loss of type safety when using custom fetch clients
- Boilerplate workarounds required for every API call
- Custom fetch clients (which are essential for auth, retries, interceptors) become impractical
- The `fetch` option in RPC client is advertised but not truly usable with real-world fetch implementations

## Possible Solutions

1. **Generic type parameter for fetch response type**
   ```typescript
   type ClientResponse<TBody, TStatus, TFormat, TFetchClient = 'native'> = ...
   ```

2. **Separate type for custom fetch clients**
   ```typescript
   type CustomClientResponse<TBody, TStatus> = TBody
   ```

3. **Configuration option to specify fetch behavior**
   ```typescript
   createClient('/', { 
     fetch: customFetch,
     fetchBehavior: 'throw-on-error' // or 'native'
   })
   ```

4. **Response transformer function**
   Allow users to provide a type-safe transformer that maps their fetch client's response to a known shape

## Environment

- Hono version: Latest
- Custom fetch client: ofetch (part of Nuxt/Nitro ecosystem)
- Use case: Nuxt 4 application with authentication, token refresh, and error handling

## Related

This affects anyone using:
- ofetch (Nuxt/Nitro)
- ky
- axios
- Any custom fetch wrapper with authentication/retry logic

The current workaround significantly reduces the developer experience and type safety that Hono's RPC client promises to deliver.

body:
## 🐛 Bug Report

**Severity:** High  
**Category:** Security - Validation Bypass  
**Location:** `src/validator/validator.ts`

**Found by:** [WhiteRose](https://github.com/shakecodeslikecray/whiterose) - AI-powered bug hunter  
**Bug ID:** WR-012

---

## 📋 Description

Validation middleware can be bypassed by accessing raw request data directly from the context object, allowing unvalidated data to reach route handlers.

---

## 🔍 Vulnerable Pattern

```typescript
app.post('/users', validator('json', userSchema), async (c) => {
  // ✅ This is validated
  const validatedData = c.req.valid('json')
  
  // ❌ But this bypasses validation!
  const rawData = await c.req.json()
  // 'rawData' contains unvalidated, potentially malicious input
})
```

---

## 💥 Impact

- **Schema validation bypass:** Malicious data can slip through
- **Type safety violations:** TypeScript types don't match runtime data
- **Security vulnerabilities:** SQL injection, XSS, etc. if raw data is used

---

## ✅ Suggested Fix

**Option 1:** Make raw access methods private after validation
**Option 2:** Add warnings in documentation about using `c.req.valid()` only
**Option 3:** Freeze/seal raw data after validation to prevent accidental access

**Documentation example:**
```typescript
// ✅ CORRECT: Always use validated data
const data = c.req.valid('json')

// ❌ WRONG: Never access raw data after validation
const raw = await c.req.json()  // Bypasses validation!
```

---

## 🔗 References

- **WhiteRose:** https://github.com/shakecodeslikecray/whiterose
- **Related:** Input validation best practices

feat: Add AES-256-GCM encrypted cookie support
body:
## Feature Request

### Summary

The current cookie helper only supports **signed cookies** (HMAC-SHA256), which provides integrity but not confidentiality — the cookie value remains readable in plaintext.

This request adds **encrypted cookie** support using **AES-256-GCM** via the Web Crypto API, providing both **confidentiality and integrity** for cookie values.

### Motivation

- Signed cookies (`setSignedCookie`) prove the value wasn't tampered with, but the value is still visible (e.g., `session=user-id-123.signature`).
- Encrypted cookies make the value opaque — useful for storing sensitive data like session tokens, user preferences, or any data that should not be readable client-side.
- AES-256-GCM is the standard choice: authenticated encryption with a single pass.

### Proposed API

Mirror the existing signed cookie API:

```ts
import {
  setEncryptedCookie,
  getEncryptedCookie,
  generateEncryptedCookie,
} from 'hono/cookie'

// Set
await setEncryptedCookie(c, 'session', 'sensitive-data', secret)

// Get (returns string | undefined | false)
const value = await getEncryptedCookie(c, secret, 'session')

// Generate without setting on response
const cookie = await generateEncryptedCookie('session', 'sensitive-data', secret)
```

### Design

- **Algorithm**: AES-256-GCM via `crypto.subtle` (multi-runtime: Node, Deno, Bun, CF Workers)
- **Key derivation**: HKDF-SHA256 from `string | BufferSource` secret (same type as signed cookies)
- **IV**: Random 12 bytes per encryption via `crypto.getRandomValues()`
- **AAD**: Cookie name bound as additional authenticated data (prevents copying encrypted values between cookie names)
- **Cookie format**: `base64(iv || ciphertext || authTag)`, URL-encoded
- **Prefix support**: Full `__Secure-` / `__Host-` prefix support
- **Return semantics**: `false` on decryption failure (tampered/wrong key), same as `getSignedCookie`

### Checklist

- [x] API mirrors existing signed cookie pattern
- [x] Uses Web Crypto API for multi-runtime compatibility
- [x] Supports cookie prefixes (`secure`, `host`)
- [x] All standard cookie options (domain, path, maxAge, expires, httpOnly, sameSite, etc.)

title: fix(cors): Vary: Origin header incorrectly appended when dynamic origin function resolves to '*'
body:
### What version of Hono are you using?

4.12.31

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

All runtimes (Bun 1.3.14, Node.js v24, Deno 2.x, Cloudflare Workers)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create a Hono app using the `cors` middleware with a dynamic origin function that resolves to `'*'` for certain requests:

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { cors } from 'hono/cors'

const app = new Hono()

app.use(
  '/api/*',
  cors({
    // Dynamic origin function returning '*'
    origin: (origin) => (origin.endsWith('.example.com') ? origin : '*'),
  })
)

app.get('/api/test', (c) => c.json({ success: true }))

// Make a request from an origin that resolves to '*'
const res = await app.request('http://localhost/api/test', {
  headers: { origin: 'http://untrusted-site.com' },
})

console.log('Access-Control-Allow-Origin:', res.headers.get('Access-Control-Allow-Origin'))
console.log('Vary:', res.headers.get('Vary'))


### What is the expected behavior?

1. When `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` is returned, `Vary: Origin` **should NOT be set**, because the response is universally valid for any origin and can be cached by CDNs without origin-based variation.
2. Per MDN specification for `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`:
   > *"Suppose the server sends a response with an Access-Control-Allow-Origin value with an explicit origin (rather than the "*" wildcard)."* -> Only then should `Vary: Origin` be appended.


### What do you see instead?

1. `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` is returned, **BUT `Vary: Origin` is still appended** to the response headers (`Vary: Origin`).
2. If `origin` returns `null` (origin rejected), `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` is omitted, but `Vary: Origin` is STILL appended unnecessarily.


### Additional information

#### Root Cause Analysis
In `src/middleware/cors/index.ts`, lines 115 and 153 evaluate whether to append `Vary: Origin` by checking:

```ts
if (opts.origin !== '*') {
  c.header('Vary', 'Origin', { append: true })
}
```

When opts.origin is a function (origin, c) => ..., typeof opts.origin is 'function'. Therefore opts.origin !== '*' always evaluates to true, regardless of what string value the function actually resolves to ('*', an explicit origin, or null).

Proposed Fix
Evaluate the resolved allowOrigin string instead of opts.origin:

```
- if (opts.origin !== '*') {
+ if (allowOrigin && allowOrigin !== '*') {
    c.header('Vary', 'Origin', { append: true })
  }

title: A function component returning an array fails with "str.search is not a function"
body:
### What version of Hono are you using? 4.12.32 ### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible) Node.js v24.13.0, also reproduced on Bun 1.3.12 ### What steps can reproduce the bug? A function component that returns an array fails to render. ```tsx import { Hono } from 'hono' const app = new Hono() const Items = () => ['a', 'b'].map((x) =>
  • {x}
    • ) app.get('/', (c) => c.html()) export default app ``` ### What is the expected behavior? Either of these, depending on which direction you prefer: 1. Returning an array stays unsupported, but the failure says so, instead of surfacing `str.search` from an internal helper. At minimum the message should name what to change. 2. `
  • a
  • b
    • ` is rendered, the same as wrapping the elements in a Fragment. `hono/jsx/dom` already renders the array-returning version this way, so today the two renderers disagree on what a component may return. ### What do you see instead? The request responds 500, and the terminal shows a message that names an internal helper: ``` TypeError: str.search is not a function ``` `JSXFunctionNode.toStringToBuffer()` in `src/jsx/base.ts` branches on the component's return value: boolean, `null`, `Promise`, `JSXNode`, number, escaped string. An array matches none of them, so it falls through to the final `else`, which calls `escapeToBuffer()` in `src/utils/html.ts`. That helper starts with `str.search(escapeRe)`, and an array has no such method. ### Additional information TypeScript rejects the same code with `TS2786: 'Items' cannot be used as a JSX component. Its return type 'Element[]' is not a valid JSX element`, so this only reaches the runtime when types are not checked. React has allowed components to return arrays since v16, so the pattern is easy to arrive at when porting. I have implemented both directions and will open a PR for each, so they can be compared side by side. They are alternatives rather than a pair: only one should be merged, and I will close the other. **1. Keeping it unsupported.** A single branch in `JSXFunctionNode.toStringToBuffer()` throws `A function component must not return an array. Wrap the elements in a Fragment: <>...`. No type changes are needed, because the type layer already rejects the code. This leaves `hono/jsx/dom` and the string renderer disagreeing, now with an explicit message rather than a confusing one. **2. Supporting the array return.** `JSXFunctionNode.toStringToBuffer()` hands arrays to `childrenToStringToBuffer()`, the path already used for array children. To make it reachable from TypeScript, `Child[]` goes into the call signature of `FC`, and `JSX.ElementType` is defined with the same return type. Since a component may be async, `Child` also has to carry `Promise`, and a resolved array is wrapped in a fragment. That is three public types, so it is your call rather than mine. Both PRs will link back to this issue.

### Summary

Link: https://docs.litestar.dev/latest/usage/dto/0-basic-use.html#improving-performance-with-the-codegen-backend

> Given a generic type, with an arbitrary number of type parameters (e.g., `GenericType[Type0, Type1, ..., TypeN])`, we use the index of the type parameter to indicate which type the exclusion should refer to. For example, a.0.b, excludes the b field from the first type parameter of a, a.1.b excludes the b field from the second type parameter of a, and so on.

But I still don't understand what `pets.0.id` means :)

Here are my questions:
1. Is `pets.0` an index of an object? For example in `[Pet(id=1, name="Dog"), Pet(id=2, name="Cat")]` will both of them not have an `id`? Or only `Dog`?
2. This sentence confuses me even more:

> Given a generic type, with an arbitrary number of type parameters (e.g., `GenericType[Type0, Type1, ..., TypeN])`, we use the index of the type parameter to indicate which type the exclusion should refer to

Because neither `User` or `Pet` is generic. They don't have any type params.

I don't have any proposals on how to fix this, because I don't understand how it works :)

title: Enhancement: Add query params to litestar.response.redirect.Redirect
body:
### Summary

I'd like to be able to specify query parameters in `Redirect.__init__`, rather than having to encode and append them to the redirect path manually.

### Basic Example

Before:
```
from urllib.parse import urlencode

from litestar.response import Redirect

params = {"key_1": "value_1", "key_2": ["value_2a", "value_2b"]}
query_string = urlencode(params)
response = Redirect(f"/my_path?{query_string}")
```

After:
```
from litestar.response import Redirect

response = Redirect("/my_path", params=params)
```

### Drawbacks and Impact

It would be easier to provide query params when redirecting to a URL.

title: Bug: ASGIApp's with custom exception handlers result in Litestar throwing `AttributeError` when an exception occurs within the ASGI APP
body:
### Description

If an ASGI App mounted using `@asgi("/", is_mount=True)` defines a custom exception handler, litestar will throw an `AttributeError` from the `litestar/middleware/_internal/exceptions/middleware.py` file when said ASGI App raises an exception.

It looks like the file takes `app: ASGIApp` but the middleware exception handling attempts to possibly treat it like `app: Litestar`. One way I have found which resolves this (and possibly introduces unintended side effects) is as follows:
```py
...

litestar_app = scope["app"]
from litestar import Litestar
if not isinstance(litestar_app, Litestar):
    # Unknown ASGI App, cannot handle automatically
    raise

if litestar_app.logging_config and (logger := litestar_app.logger):
    self.handle_exception_logging(logger=logger, logging_config=litestar_app.logging_config, scope=scope)

...
```

### URL to code causing the issue

_No response_

### MCVE

```python
from litestar import Litestar, asgi
from litestar.types import Receive, Scope, Send
from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException

title: Bug: `Example` class is missing an ID field
body:
### Description

The `litestar.openapi.spec.Example` class is missing an `id` field that would allow IDs to be customized when they are autogenerated when you provide multiple `Example`s to `ResponseSpec`.

As a workaround, I have had to set the `summary` field of `Example`s and then use the below custom code to monkey patch my OpenAPI specification:
```
import re

from litestar import Litestar


def _fix_autogenerated_example_ids(spec: dict) -> None:
    """Fix autogenerated example IDs in the provided OpenAPI schema in place,
    preferring to use the example's `summary` field if one exists, otherwise
    using `example` if there is only one example, and otherwise using `example #<index>`
    for each example where there are multiple examples.
    
    See https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar/issues/4013"""

    if isinstance(spec, dict):
        for k, v in spec.items():
            # Filter for example objects.
            if k == "examples" and isinstance(v, dict):
                # Filter for example IDs matching the format `<nonwhitespace_lowercase_alphabetic_string>-example-<digit/s>`.
                if all(re.search(r"[a-z]+-example-\d+", k2) for k2 in v.keys()):
                    # If every example has a `summary` field, use that as the new example ID.
                    if len({e["summary"] for e in v.values() if "summary" in e}) == len(v.values()):
                        new_examples = {}

                        for example in v.values():
                            new_examples[example["summary"]] = example
                    
                    else:
                        # If there's only one example, use the word "example" as the new example ID.
                        if len(v) == 1:
                            new_examples = {"example": list(v.values())[0]}

                        # Otherwise, use the format `example #<index>` as the new example ID.
                        else:
                            new_examples = {}

                            for idx, example in enumerate(v.values(), start=1):
                                new_examples[f"example #{idx}"] = example

                    spec[k] = new_examples
            
            # Recursively fix example IDs in nested objects.
            _fix_autogenerated_example_ids(v)
    
    # Recursively fix example IDs in nested lists.
    elif isinstance(spec, list):
        for elm in spec:
            _fix_autogenerated_example_ids(elm)


def gen_openapi(app: Litestar) -> dict:
    """Generate the OpenAPI schema for the provided Litestar application, applying necessary transformations to the schema."""
    
    # Generate the OpenAPI schema.
    schema = app.openapi_schema
    schema = schema.to_schema()

    # Fix example IDs autogenerated by Litestar.
    _fix_autogenerated_example_ids(schema)

    return schema
```

title: Enhancement: Support `Websocket Denial Response` ASGI extension
body:
### Description

Litestar does not support raising a `HTTPException` correctly or sending a `Response` from a websocket handler when the ASGI Server supports the `Websocket Denial Response` Extension.

Currently raising a `HTTPException` will always result in a Status Code `403`.

The ASGI spec supports the [Websocket Denial Response](https://asgi.readthedocs.io/en/latest/extensions.html#websocket-denial-response) extension. The `websocket.http.response` key will be present in the scope extensions dict when the ASGI Server supports this type of response. 

Since this seems to be the default for `Uvicorn` and others when started with Websockets support, and even though the ASGI Spec considers this use-case niche, I decided to open a bug report rather than a Feature-Request, as the template allows for more info, however it's a bit of both.

Starlette has more information on how they handle this: https://www.starlette.io/websockets/

I have provided a minimal Starlette example as a comparison:
```py
from starlette.applications import Starlette
from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException
from starlette.routing import WebSocketRoute
from starlette.websockets import WebSocket


async def connect_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket) -> None:
    raise HTTPException(detail="TeaPot", status_code=418)


app = Starlette(routes=[WebSocketRoute("/connect", connect_endpoint)])
```

From what I gather, this is due to how the internal exception middleware handles websocket exceptions: https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar/blob/66d7dfa3851486376908deb32787d7228ce723da/litestar/middleware/_internal/exceptions/middleware.py#L230

Since I don't know the codebase too well, I also decided I wouldn't open a PR.

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

import litestar
from litestar import Litestar, WebSocket
from litestar.exceptions import HTTPException


if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from litestar.types import WebSocketScope


@litestar.websocket("/connect")
async def websocket_endpoint(socket: WebSocket[Any, Any, Any]) -> None:
    scope: WebSocketScope = socket.scope

    # Check if Websocket Denial Extension is present...
    print("websocket.http.response" in scope.get("extensions", {}))  # type: ignore
    raise HTTPException(detail="TeaPot", status_code=418)


app = Litestar(route_handlers=[websocket_endpoint])
```

2. Attempt to connect to `/connect` via Websocket.

async def main() -> None:

title: Bug: Misleading and unhelpful error message upon `ImportError` with `--app` argument to CLI
body:
### Description

When using `litestar run` with application lookup through a directory (e.g. the CWD), and an `ImportError` happens, you get a normal traceback, showing exactly what is going on. However, if you instead import the app through the environment, as `litestar --app "app_module:app" run`, and any kind of `ImportError` happens, the only thing you get is this:
```
Using Litestar app from env: 'app_module:app'
 Invalid argument passed --app 'app_module:app': Module not found
```
In particular, this misleadingly seems to suggests that `app_module` cannot be found. In reality, you get the same error message no matter which module caused the `ImportError`. This issue is exacerbated by the fact that these errors typically happen due to a packaging problem, which often is only identified in CI testing or the staging environment, where direct analysis of the issue is not possible.

# the following module does not exist, highlighting an ImportError with a dependency.
import does_not_exist

    return {"hello": "world"}


app = Litestar(route_handlers=[hello_world])

title: Bug: Request sometimes has wrong accept header when running with hypercorn 0.17
body:
### Description

I've reported this as [hypercorn/301](https://github.com/pgjones/hypercorn/issues/301) but suspect Litestar could be the underlying cause, hence this issue.

We have a Litestar WSGI server running with hypercorn. This has worked just fine until Python packages were recently upgraded as part of a general update -- after this the server occasionally sends the wrong response to a request. 

Our code uses content-negotiation, based on the request's `Accept` header, to determine the response -- comparing browser logs with a server trace, we can see the client consistently sending `Accept: application/json`; the server though only sees `application/json`  for about about three out of four requests; at other times, values seen have included `*/*`, `image/webp,*/*`, and `image/avif,image/webp,image/apng,image/svg+xml,image/*,*/*;q=0.8`. 

Prior to the update we were using hypercorn 0.16.0; the update took this to 0.17.3. We've seen this with all browsers so far tested -- Chrome, Firefox and Safari; the server string reported back to the browser is `hypercorn-h11`.

I've debugged this by freezing our code and all package versions, apart from hypercorn, using this from a git controlled working directory. Binary searching of commits has found that the accept header is correct in the Litestar request until commit [d1c1a23](https://github.com/pgjones/hypercorn/commit/d1c1a23ae2a24fc2cd059a51b844013725993532) -- this commit added support for lifespan state. Looking at code changes, this support appears to pass `state` around without modifying anything.

Debugging with print statements in hypercorn, at the point where a HTTP stream is handled, finds `scope['headers']` correctly includes `(b'accept', b'application/json')` but the headers contained in `scope['state']` have `'accept': 'image/webp,*/*',`. 

Why does a scope's state appear to have details of a prior request? And does Litestar prioritise headers in a scope's state over those in the HTTP request?

title: Bug: Empty strings in multipart/form-data requests are converted to None
body:
### Description

Empty strings are parsed correctly when using `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. However, when using `multipart/form-data`, they instead get converted to `None`.

This is due to `litestar/_multipart.py:112`:

```
if isinstance(data, UploadFile):
    await data.seek(0)
    fields[segment.name].append(data)
elif data:  # here, data is a bytearray
    fields[segment.name].append(data.decode(segment.charset or "utf-8"))
else:
    fields[segment.name].append(None)
```

Because `data` is tested using boolean conversion instead of explicit comparison,`''` (which converts to the empty bytearray) will fail the check and the `else` branch will be taken.

I'm willing to create a PR for this, but it would be a breaking change.

### URL to code causing the issue

_No response_

### MCVE

```python
from typing import Annotated

from litestar import Litestar
from litestar import post
from litestar.enums import RequestEncodingType
from litestar.params import Body
from pydantic import BaseModel


class Data(BaseModel):
    value: str | None


@post("/f", sync_to_thread=False)
def f(data: Annotated[Data, Body(media_type=RequestEncodingType.URL_ENCODED)]) -> bool:
    return data.value is not None


@post("/g", sync_to_thread=False)
def g(data: Annotated[Data, Body(media_type=RequestEncodingType.MULTI_PART)]) -> bool:

app = Litestar(route_handlers=[f, g])

title: Enhancement: allow event to be emitted without any listeners
body:
### Summary

Currently, emitting an event that has no listeners results in error raised here:


https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar/blob/04e12b886a10e9e99a6ea02c5339ed0058cee2a2/litestar/events/emitter.py#L112-L130

This isn't ideal because the code that calls `EventEmitter.emit` has to know whether or not there are listeners attached to the event it's emitting. In my use case, the code path that emits an event is decoupled from the submodules that contain the listeners. The listeners may be put in production _after_ the code that emits it, so there's no guarantee that a listener exists for a given event.

With the current API, I have to comment out the code that emits the event, which breaks the fire-and-forget ergonomics.

### Basic Example

MRE:

```python
from litestar.events import EventListener, SimpleEventEmitter

EVENT_ID = "foo"


@EventListener(EVENT_ID)
def foo_listener() -> None:
    print("foo received")


async def main():
    # Succeeds
    async with SimpleEventEmitter(listeners=[foo_listener]) as emitter:
        emitter.emit(EVENT_ID)
    # => foo received

    # Errors
    async with SimpleEventEmitter(listeners=[]) as emitter:
        emitter.emit(EVENT_ID)
    # => litestar.exceptions.http_exceptions.ImproperlyConfiguredException: 500: no event listeners are registered for event ID: foo


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import asyncio

    asyncio.run(main())
```

title: Bug: Pydantic `RootModel` incorrectly gets its dummy `root` field included in the OpenAPI schema
body:
### Description

Title really says it all. Pydantic supports defining root models[^1], which have a top-level dummy `root` key, under which the actual annotation for the model is defined. This is particularly useful for defining discriminated unions[^2] inside a container, like a list, that is itself used to annotate a field in a Pydantic model.

A model that inherits from `RootModel` gets its `__pydantic_root_model__` attribute set to `True` under the hood, so that's one way Litestar could extract that information.

[^1]: https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/models/#rootmodel-and-custom-root-types
[^2]: https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/fields/#discriminator


### URL to code causing the issue

_No response_

### MCVE

```python
# main.py

from typing import List
from litestar import Litestar, get
from pydantic import BaseModel, RootModel


class MyModel(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str


class MyRootModel(RootModel[List[MyModel]]):
    """Root model for the API."""


@get("/", sync_to_thread=True)
def get_data() -> MyRootModel:
    """Get data from the API."""
    return MyRootModel(
        root=[
            MyModel(id=1, name="one"),
            MyModel(id=2, name="two"),
        ]
    )


app = Litestar(route_handlers=[get_data])
```

### Steps to reproduce

Start the app:

```shell
uv run uvicorn main:app --reload
```

The response is the list you would expect:

```console
$ http -p=b http://127.0.0.1:8000/
[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "name": "one"
    },
    {
        "id": 2,
        "name": "two"
    }
]
```

but the OpenAPI schema is nested under the `root` key:

```console
$ http -p=b http://127.0.0.1:8000/schema/openapi.json | jq .components.schemas.MyRootModel
{
  "properties": {
    "root": {
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/components/schemas/MyModel"
      },
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "root"

}

title: FEAT: Adding --json output option in /cli/core .py on routes command
body:
### Summary

# Feature Request: Add `--json` Option to `routes` Command

## Description

Currently, the `routes` command outputs the list of application routes in a human-readable table format.  
It would be useful to add a `--json` flag to allow users to export the routes in **JSON format**, making it easier to programmatically consume the route information.

## Proposed Solution

- Add a `--json` option to the `routes` CLI command.
- When `--json` is provided, output the list of routes as a JSON array instead of the default table.
- Ensure that the JSON output includes all relevant route details (e.g., path, methods, name, handler, etc.).
- Update or add tests to validate JSON output.

## Benefits

- Programmatic access to route data for tooling or documentation generation.
- Improves automation and integration with other tools.

## Additional Context

This feature is especially useful for larger applications where manual inspection of routes is cumbersome, or when generating automated documentation.

### Basic Example

## Example Usage

```bash
$ litestar routes --json
[
  {
    "name": h.name,
    "path": h.paths,
    "handler": h.handler_name,
    "methods": sorted(h.http_methods),
    "async": inspect.iscoroutinefunction(unwrap_partial(h.fn))  
  },
]
```


### Drawbacks and Impact

## Drawbacks

Some drawbacks only occurs in particular cases.

- Potential for sensitive information exposure
- Performance impact
- Maintenance overhead

title: Enhancement: Provide a mechanism to return a string that is _not_ treated as preencoded
body:
### Summary

Right now, when a method returns a string, that string is returned directly to the client without JSON or msgpack escaping. This is demonstrated by the following test case:

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
from typing import Literal
from litestar import Litestar, MediaType, get
from litestar.testing import TestClient

@get("/str")
def str_handler() -> str:
    return "enabled"

@get("/literal")
def literal_handler() -> Literal["enabled", "disabled"]:
    return "enabled"

@get("/literal-typed", media_type=MediaType.JSON)
def literal_handler_typed() -> Literal["enabled", "disabled"]:
    return "enabled"

app = Litestar(route_handlers=[str_handler, literal_handler, literal_handler_typed])

with TestClient(app=app) as client:
    r1 = client.get("/str")
    r2 = client.get("/literal")
    r3 = client.get("/literal-typed")

    # How can I make a method that returns a Literal have that escaped be valid in the MediaType?
    print(f"str return:           content-type={r1.headers['content-type']}, body={r1.content!r}")
    print(f"Literal return:       content-type={r2.headers['content-type']}, body={r2.content!r}")
    print(f"Literal typed return: content-type={r3.headers['content-type']}, body={r3.content!r}")
```

...which emits:

```none
str return:           content-type=text/plain; charset=utf-8, body=b'enabled'
Literal return:       content-type=application/json, body=b'enabled'
Literal typed return: content-type=application/json, body=b'enabled'
```

Note that in the literal cases, `enabled` is returned with a content-type of `application/json`, but (lacking quotes) this isn't actually valid JSON and will fail to parse.

---

For Litestar 3.0, when a compatibility break is possible, it should be necessary to return `msgspec.Raw[str]` to get the current/2.0 behavior -- by default, returning a `str` should cause that string to be encoded, consistently with how other datatypes are handled.

For Litestar 2.x, we should consider an interface to specify that a value _is not_ raw, even if it's of type `str` or `bytes`, so clients are able to opt out of the responsibility of encoding.

### Basic Example

If the proposed feature were implemented in the mechanism proposed for 3.0, output of the test above instead would be:

```none
str return:           content-type=application/json, body=b'"enabled"'
Literal return:       content-type=application/json, body=b'"enabled"'
Literal typed return: content-type=application/json, body=b'"enabled"'
```

...whereas a return type of `msgspec.Raw[str]` would be necessary for `body=b'enabled'` to be returned.

### Drawbacks and Impact

- Implementing this properly is a compatibility break.
- For any interim 2.x interface, we would need to decide whether to drop it in the migration to 3.0 (creating an extra migration step for users) or keep it (and add extra complexity)

### Unresolved questions

_No response_

title: Bug: Exceptions raised in exception handlers bubble up to the ASGI web server
body:
### Description

When an exception handler defined on a child (e.g. an individual route handler) raises an exception, I would expect that exception to bubble up to any exception handlers defined on its parents (e.g. the containing controller, and eventually to the `Litestar` instance) so that they can handle them, and in any case for such exceptions to be caught by Litestar's "last chance" handler.

However, what actually happens is that once an exception handler raises an exception, it propagates all the way to the hosting ASGI server (in my case, `uvicorn`), with no way to catch it.

### URL to code causing the issue

_No response_

### MCVE

```python
from litestar import Litestar
from litestar import Response
from litestar import get


def parent_exception_handler(request, exc) -> Response[str]:
    return Response("parent")


def child_exception_handler(request, exc) -> Response[str]:
    raise ValueError()


@get("/", exception_handlers={Exception: child_exception_handler}, sync_to_thread=False)
def root() -> None:
    raise ValueError()


app = Litestar(route_handlers=[root], exception_handlers={Exception: parent_exception_handler})
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start Litestar.
2. Navigate to `/`.


### Screenshots

_No response_

### Logs

```text

body:
### Description

PydanticDTO fails to validate request payloads containing list[NestedModel] | None fields, while native Pydantic handles them correctly.

**MCVE reproduces the issue.** 
**Expected Behaviour of the MCVE:**
Both endpoints should return 201 Created since the payload is valid.

The /dto endpoint returns 400 Bad Request while the native pydantic(/native) endpoint returns 201 as expected:

      "type": "model_type",

title: Bug: after_request does not trigger on responses returned from exception handlers
body:
### Description

If an exception is raised and mapped to a response by an exception handler, `after_request` is not called on it.

I'm aware that this may be by design (because either the exception handler can catch an exception raised in an `after_request` hook, or the `after_request` hook can modify the response; anything else risks infinite recursion). However, _personally_, it makes more sense to me for the `after_request` hook to run later.

In any case, even if this is intended behaviour (and this may be a better fit for a docs issue), what is supposed to happen is nonobvious, since, AFAIK, there is no diagram on the Litestar website that shows the various Litestar components a request travels through from the point it's assembled from ASGI events to the point it gets turned back into ASGI events (e.g. `before_request` -> router -> route handler -> ....

title: Enhancement: Support Python 3.14 free-threaded
body:
### Summary `litestar[standard]` has a dependency on `fast-query-parsers`, which publishes abi3-compatible wheels. Unfortunately:

The ultimate problem is that CPython does not yet offer a stable ABI on the free-threaded build. See this CPython issue for more details. This means it's not yet possible to build an extension that any CPython version can import and instead libraries have to distribute one wheel for each version of free-threaded CPython. A future version of CPython will likely support a new version of the stable ABI that works correctly with both the GIL-enabled and free-threaded builds.

(from [Quansight Labs' Free-Threading Guide](https://py-free-threading.github.io/faq/#what-does-py_limited_api-is-currently-incompatible-with-py_gil_disabled-mean)) I opened https://github.com/litestar-org/fast-query-parsers/pull/36 to start building those missing wheels. ### Basic Example ```console $ uvx -p 3.14t --with 'litestar[standard]' python -c 'import litestar' Built fast-query-parsers==1.0.3 Built httptools==0.7.1 × Failed to download and build `fast-query-parsers==1.0.3` ╰─▶ The built wheel `fast_query_parsers-1.0.3-cp38-abi3-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl` is not compatible with the current Python 3.14 on macos aarch64 help: `fast-query-parsers` (v1.0.3) was included because `litestar[standard]` (v2.19.0) depends on `fast-query-parsers` ``` ### Drawbacks and Impact _No response_ ### Unresolved questions _No response_

title: Bug: inconsistent type of Decimal in JSON and OpenAPI schema
body:
### Description

When using `msgpsec` and a `decimal.Decimal`, the default serialization format is supposed to be string. (This can be adjusted via a parameter in the JSON encoder https://jcristharif.com/msgspec/api.html#msgspec.json.Encoder but is not recommended because of precision losses.) This matches the behavior observed in the JSON return value of a route in Litestar, which correctly returns a string. However, the generated OpenAPI schema assigns `number` as the type of the `Decimal` the value.

If I understand the codebase correctly, this inconsistency is created during the OpenAPI schema generation. `Decimal`s are handled by the same function as `float` and `int`, which does not match the assumption of `msgspec`.

### URL to code causing the issue

https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar/blob/32c595ba13873c3992e35c33686d63f5ccc49f7d/litestar/_openapi/schema_generation/schema.py#L514

### MCVE

```python
from decimal import Decimal

from litestar import Litestar, get
import msgspec

class HelloWorld(msgspec.Struct):
    value: Decimal

@get("/")
async def hello_world() -> HelloWorld:
    """Handler function that returns a greeting dictionary."""
    return HelloWorld(value=Decimal("1.001"))


app = Litestar(route_handlers=[hello_world])
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the MCVE
2. Send `curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/` and receive `{"value":"1.001"}`
3. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8000/schema` in browser and see `value: number`

title: Bug: `AllowedHostsMiddleware` rejects valid hosts when the `Host` header includes a port
body:
### Description

`AllowedHostsMiddleware` used to strip the port from the `Host` header before matching it against the allowed-hosts regex. As of 2.22.0 it matches the **full, un-stripped** header, so a request with `Host: localhost:8000` no longer matches an allowed host of `localhost` and is rejected with `400 - invalid host header`.

The host check works correctly in production behind a proxy (where `Host` is the bare domain with no port), which is likely why this has gone unnoticed — it only manifests when the `Host` header carries a port.

### Root cause

The port-strip was lost in [`c4189610` ("fix: fix typing after merge")](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar/commit/c4189610), a follow-up to the intentional `x-forwarded-host` removal. The walrus now binds `host` to the **un-stripped** header value; `host.split(":")[0]` survives only as the truthiness guard on the left of the `and`, while `fullmatch(host)` receives the value with the port still attached:

```python
# before (2.21.x) — port stripped, then matched
if host := headers.get("host").split(":")[0]:
    if self.allowed_hosts_regex.fullmatch(host):

# after (2.22.0+) — `host` keeps the port; the strip only gates the `if`
if (host := headers.get("host")) is not None and host.split(":")[0]:
    if self.allowed_hosts_regex.fullmatch(host):   # matches "localhost:8000"
```

### Suggested fix

Match against the port-stripped value while keeping the `None` guard, e.g.:

```python
if (raw_host := headers.get("host")) is not None and (host := raw_host.split(":")[0]):
    if self.allowed_hosts_regex.fullmatch(host):
```

### URL to code causing the issue

_No response_

### MCVE

```python
from litestar import Litestar, get
from litestar.config.allowed_hosts import AllowedHostsConfig
from litestar.testing import TestClient


@get("/")
async def handler() -> str:
    return "ok"


app = Litestar(
    route_handlers=[handler],
    allowed_hosts=AllowedHostsConfig(allowed_hosts=["localhost"]),
)


def test_host_with_port_is_allowed() -> None:
    # base_url drives the Host header -> "localhost:8000"
    with TestClient(app=app, base_url="http://localhost:8000") as client:
        response = client.get("/")
    assert response.status_code == 200  # passes on 2.21.x, fails (400) on >= 2.22.0
```

### Steps to reproduce

### Expected behavior
`Host: localhost:8000` matches the allowed host `localhost` (port stripped before matching), and the request returns `200`. This is the 2.21.x behavior, and matches the convention used by Django's `ALLOWED_HOSTS` and Starlette's `TrustedHostMiddleware`.

### Actual behavior
The request is rejected with `400 - {"message":"invalid host header"}` because the port is included in the matched value.

title: Bug: Controller `dto` is not used as fallback for response serialization when `return_dto` is omitted
body:
### Description

### Summary

According to the documentation, when `return_dto` is not provided, the `dto` should also be used to serialize the handler's return value.

However, this does not seem to happen when using `SQLAlchemyDTO` from Advanced Alchemy.

Documentation:

https://docs.litestar.dev/2/usage/dto/0-basic-use.html#dto-layer-parameters

> If no `return_dto` is declared on the handler, `dto` is also used to encode the return data.

---

### Versions

- Litestar: 2.24.0
- Advanced Alchemy: 1.11.0
- SQLAlchemy: 2.0.51
- Python: 3.14.6

---

### Minimal example

```python
from litestar import Controller, get
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar import (
    SQLAlchemyDTO,
    SQLAlchemyDTOConfig,
)


class UserDTO(SQLAlchemyDTO[User]):
    config = SQLAlchemyDTOConfig(
        exclude={
            User.id,
            User.code,
        }
    )


class UserController(Controller):
    path = "/users"
    dto = UserDTO

    @get()
    async def list_users(self) -> list[User]:
        return await service.list()
```

---

### Expected behavior

The response should be serialized using UserDTO, excluding the configured fields, because no return_dto is explicitly provided.

### Actual behavior

The response is serialized with all model fields. If I explicitly set:

```python
return_dto = UserDTO
```

everything works as expected.

### Additional information

Printing the controller attributes shows:

```python
print(UserController.dto)
print(UserController.return_dto)
```

Output:

```python
<class '__main__.UserDTO'>
<member 'return_dto' of 'Controller' objects>
```

---

This makes me wonder whether the documented fallback from dto to return_dto is not being applied.
Could this be a regression, or is the documentation outdated for SQLAlchemyDTO?

If this behavior belongs to Advanced Alchemy rather than Litestar, I'd appreciate it if you could point me to the appropriate repository.

Thank you!

title: Enhancement(CI): Zizmor baseline policy + Dependabot/uv cooldown (follow-up to #4489)
body:
### Summary

Follow-up to #4489 to agree on a baseline for adding [Zizmor](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor) (GitHub Actions static analysis), plus a couple of related Dependabot/pre-commit hardening items. Opening this per @cofin's request so the direction gets a review before I put up the PR.

Everything here is a recommendation — happy to go whichever way maintainers prefer. The actual config and workflow fixes land in a follow-up PR.

### Basic Example

**1. How to run it**
- `pre-commit` hook ([`zizmor-pre-commit`](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor-pre-commit)) so findings show up locally.
- For CI, two ways to run it:
  1. **CLI directly** — `uvx zizmor` (we already use `uv`), then upload the SARIF ourselves. More control, one more action to pin.
  2. **[`zizmorcore/zizmor-action`](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor-action)** — wraps the run + SARIF upload for us. Less boilerplate, but it's another third-party action to SHA-pin and trust.
  Either way results land in the Security tab and as PR annotations. Slight lean toward the CLI for control, but no strong opinion — maintainer's call.
- I'd make it **blocking** on PRs. Most of the findings below are mechanical to fix, so it's a one-time cleanup rather than an ongoing tax.
- I'd stick with the default (`Regular`) persona — the full run below came from it, so `pedantic` doesn't add anything for the baseline. Easy to tighten later.

**2. Action pinning (`unpinned-uses`)**
Actions are pinned to tags today (e.g. `actions/checkout@v7.0.1`), and Zizmor flags 52 of those as High. Given the recent run of supply-chain incidents (`tj-actions/changed-files`, etc.), I'd pin everything to a full commit SHA with a version comment and let Dependabot keep the SHAs fresh:

```yaml
# .github/zizmor.yml
rules:
  unpinned-uses:
    config:
      policies:
        "*": hash-pin
```

Third-party actions in the tree: `astral-sh/setup-uv`, `JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action`, `codecov/codecov-action`, `dawidd6/action-download-artifact`, `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish`, `ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres`. No `litestar-org/*` actions are used. If you'd rather keep GitHub's own actions on tags, `"actions/*": ref-pin` carves those out — the rule is per-org, so the "some like hashes, some don't" thing is fully configurable.

**3. What a real run turns up**
88 findings total (58 High / 17 Medium / 13 Low), all at the default persona:

| Rule | Count | Severity | Where | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `unpinned-uses` | 52 | High | all workflows | SHA-pin (see above) |
| `excessive-permissions` | 17 | Medium | ci, publish, pr-merged, pr-title | add least-privilege `permissions:` blocks |
| `artipacked` | 13 | Low | ci, docs, notify-released-issues, publish, test | `persist-credentials: false` on checkouts that don't push |
| `cache-poisoning` | 2 | High | docs.yml, publish.yml | guard `actions/cache` on the release paths |
| `template-injection` | 2 | High | notify-released-issues.yml, test.yml | move `${{ github.* }}` into `env:` |
| `dangerous-triggers` | 1 | High | docs-preview.yml (`workflow_run`) | audit (already partly hardened) |
| `github-env` | 1 | High | docs-preview.yml | avoid untrusted writes to `$GITHUB_ENV`/`$GITHUB_PATH` |

Goal is a small `.github/zizmor.yml` where any suppression carries an inline `# reason`, so the policy explains itself.

**4. Dependabot (not Zizmor, but same theme)**
`dependabot.yml` only watches `github-actions` today (7-day cooldown). Two gaps:
- Add a `uv` ecosystem — our Python deps (`uv.lock`) aren't watched at all.
- Put a cooldown on third-party updates but let litestar-org's own packages (Advanced Alchemy, Polyfactory, …) through without the delay, via `cooldown.exclude:`:

```yaml
- package-ecosystem: "uv"
  directory: "/"
  schedule: { interval: "daily" }
  cooldown:
    default-days: 7
    exclude: ["advanced-alchemy", "polyfactory"]  # + rest of litestar-org packages
```

Same exclusion could apply to the existing `github-actions` cooldown.

**5. `.pre-commit-config.yaml`**
Zizmor doesn't scan this, but it's the same pinning story — hooks are tag-pinned (`rev: v5.0.0`, …), and a bad hook runs on every contributor's machine and in CI. I'd pin `rev:` to SHAs to match the actions policy. One catch: Dependabot has no pre-commit ecosystem, so keeping them fresh means either [`pre-commit.ci`](https://pre-commit.ci/) or Renovate — worth deciding who owns those bumps.

### Drawbacks and Impact

- SHA-pinning is less readable and adds Dependabot PRs (cooldown + grouping keep that in check).
- Turning CI blocking means one upfront cleanup pass: 52 hash-pins (mostly mechanical), 17 permission blocks, 13 `persist-credentials`, and ~6 real-logic findings.
- One extra tool in the chain, but Zizmor is self-contained and low-maintenance.
- Net win for a widely-depended-on library.

Optional extras worth a look:
- [OpenSSF Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard-action) — pairs well, feeds the same code-scanning UI.
- Set the repo's default `GITHUB_TOKEN` to read-only (a settings toggle) — pairs with the permissions work and the immutable-releases item in #4489.
- Dependabot grouped updates + an `open-pull-requests-limit` once `uv` is watched.

### Unresolved questions

- Hash-pin all actions, or keep `actions/*` on tags?
- Run it via the CLI (`uvx zizmor`) or [`zizmorcore/zizmor-action`](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor-action)?
- Blocking vs advisory to start, and do we want the SARIF upload?
- Fix the 6 real-logic High findings in the same PR, or split them out?
- Which litestar-org packages should be excluded from the cooldown?
- SHA-pin the pre-commit hooks too — and if so, `pre-commit.ci` or Renovate for the bumps?
- Any appetite for the optional extras above?

title: `{slug:str}/hello` shadowed by `{path:path}` catch-all — no backtracking in routing trie
body:
### Description

Description

When a `{path:path}` catch-all route and a more specific param-first route with a static suffix (e.g. `{slug:str}/hello`) are both registered, the catch-all always wins and the specific route is never matched, regardless of registration order.

This affects CMS-style applications where a catch-all permalink resolver (`{path:path}`) needs to coexist with specific param-first routes.

Static-first routes (e.g. `/hello/{slug}` or `/t/{slug}`) work fine alongside `{path:path}` because static children are checked before the path-parameter sentinel in the trie. The problem is specific to **param-first + static-suffix** patterns.


### URL to code causing the issue

_No response_

### MCVE

```python
from litestar import Litestar, get

@get("/{slug:str}/hello", name="specific")
async def specific(slug: str) -> str:
    return f"specific: {slug}"

@get("/{path:path}", name="catch_all")
async def catch_all(path: str) -> str:
    return f"catch_all: {path}"

app = Litestar([specific, catch_all])
```

### Steps to reproduce

Run the app

title: Bug(channels): single exception in backend.publish breaks all subsequent events publishing
body:
### Description

If single exception(e.g. network failure) happens in the `backend.publish`, `backend._pub_worker` dies, causing ignoring all subsequent events that will be published + deadlock on shutdown(since the plugin tries to empty the queue before shutdown)

### URL to code causing the issue

_No response_

### MCVE

```python
import asyncio
from collections.abc import Iterable
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock

from anyio import fail_after

from litestar.channels import ChannelsPlugin
from litestar.channels.backends.memory import MemoryChannelsBackend


class StubMemoryChannelBackend(MemoryChannelsBackend):
    def __init__(self, history: int = 0) -> None:
        super().__init__(history)
        self._counter = 0

    async def publish(self, data: bytes, channels: Iterable[str]) -> None:
        if self._counter == 0:
            raise RuntimeError("Network lag")
        self._counter += 1
        await super().publish(data, channels)


async def test_deadlock_on_shutdown():
    plugin = ChannelsPlugin(arbitrary_channels_allowed=True, backend=StubMemoryChannelBackend())
    with fail_after(1):
        async with plugin:
            plugin.publish("test", "test")
    # TimeoutError (during __aexit__ --> _on_shutdown)


async def test_single_exception_suppress_all_publishes():
    plugin = ChannelsPlugin(arbitrary_channels_allowed=True, backend=StubMemoryChannelBackend())
    async with plugin:
        plugin.publish("test", "test")
        sub = await plugin.subscribe("42")
        plugin.publish("42", "42")  # Stub backend does not break that, but ...
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(sub._queue.get(), timeout=1)  # TimeoutError
        except TimeoutError:
            print(
                "Backend available now but event isn't published "
                "because _pub_worker is broken since it doesn't handle exceptions"
            )
            plugin._on_shutdown = AsyncMock() # just to exit from context manager without the deadlock


asyncio.run(test_deadlock_on_shutdown())
asyncio.run(test_single_exception_suppress_all_publishes())
```

title: Bug(channels): deadlock when history exceeds subscriber_max_backlog with "backoff" strategy
body:
### Description

If `subscriber_backlog_strategy = "backoff"` and the `history` argument passed to `subscribe` exceeds `subscriber_max_backlog` constructor argument (and backend should have corresponding quantity of events)  deadlock happens during `subscribe`. This occurs since `put_subscriber_history` uses a blocking `await subscriber.put` call but at this moment nobody can consume events from the subscriber's queue.

The same deadlock happens in `ChannelsPlugin._ws_handler_func`, where `put_subscriber_history` is awaited before entering `subscriber.run_in_background` context manager which is the only consumer.

### URL to code causing the issue

_No response_

### MCVE

```python
import asyncio

from litestar.channels import ChannelsPlugin
from litestar.channels.backends.memory import MemoryChannelsBackend


async def test_deadlock_on_subscription():
    plugin = ChannelsPlugin(
        backend=MemoryChannelsBackend(history=20),
        subscriber_max_backlog=10,
        arbitrary_channels_allowed=True,
    )

    async with plugin:
        for i in range(20):
            await plugin.wait_published(f"event_{i}", "42")
        await asyncio.wait_for(plugin.subscribe("42", history=20), timeout=1.0)  # TimeoutError


asyncio.run(test_deadlock_on_subscription())
```

title: The `wrap` parameter for `OptionList` no longer works
body:
Starting in July 2023 (cb819faa37f76d03a6b0de202f6a6bfac2898567 ) `OptionList` has had a parameter to control if options should auto-wrap or not. As of Textual 1.0 it would appear that this parameter is now a no-op. Setting it to `False` has no effect and, after a brief look at the `OptionList` code, I can't see the value being actually used any more.

This will also affect `SelectionList` as it is designed to work as a non-wrapping descendent of `OptionList`.

This does, of course, potentially break the layout of any application that is relying on an `OptionList` that truncates rather than wraps its `Option`s.

A quick jog back through the blame history suggests that the regression started around here: 1a5fbb3b357395c6cb8d1ae377395f37bf86ee56

title: Apps hang temporarily on resume from sleep
body:
If a Textual app is suspended for some reason - typically because the device it's running on goes to sleep - then it will temporarily hang on resume from sleep and refuse to update or accept input. This is typically a minor stutter after a brief sleep; after being left overnight it can be several seconds; left for long enough it becomes minutes.

This occurs because of the loop here: https://github.com/Textualize/textual/blob/f5be1b7aba017b3489824fbcf51b5f8b0820a4ee/src/textual/timer.py#L152-L157

If a timer with skip enabled has fallen behind, then it busy loops until it catches up. This is fine if it's only a little behind, but rapidly becomes expensive if it's a lot behind. This busy looping behaviour happens in, for example, the `"screen_update"` timer which fires every frame. An app which has been suspended racks up about five million ticks a day, enough to produce noticeable lag while the busy loop catches up.

This is easy enough to fix - just calculate the next required timer fire rather than busy looping.

title: CONTRIBUTE.md references deprecated 'poetry shell'
body:
In CONTRIBUTE.md's Setup section, users are instructed to use `poetry shell` to activate the virtual environment.

Poetry released a major upgrade to [2.0.0](https://python-poetry.org/blog/announcing-poetry-2.0.0/) in early January. This introduced a breaking change where the `poetry shell` command was removed completely.  

The [official documentation now recommends](https://python-poetry.org/docs/managing-environments/#activating-the-environment) either passing the command `poetry env activate` to the shell, or installing the [poetry-plugin-shell](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-plugin-shell) to add this command back to Poetry.

Poetry itself is a bit vague on the issue when it mentions none of these directly in response to `poetry shell`.

```
~/s/textual (main)> poetry shell

The command "shell" does not exist.

Did you mean one of these?
    self show
    self sync
    show
    self add
    self install
    install
    self lock
    help
```   


This will need to be added to the documentation rather than replacing the old command, as not all OS have added the new version of Poetry to their stable repos yet (Debian Bookworm naturally being one that I've found at least).  

**ETA:** There's also a [fix](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/issues/10084) to an [issue](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/issues/10084) for bash/fish/zsh shells awaiting the [2.1.0 release](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/10154) as currently `poetry env activate` doesn't act like old `poetry shell` where it created a virtual environment for you if one did not already exist (have to `poetry env use` [as described](https://python-poetry.org/docs/managing-environments/#switching-between-environments) on official website first).

title: A screen that is pushed via a command palette callback does not receive the push_screen callback
body:
Have you checked closed issues? Yes

Have you checked against the most recent version of Textual? Yes

Please give a brief but clear explanation of the issue. If you can, include a complete working example that demonstrates the bug. **Check it can run without modifications.**

A screen pushed inside a `CommandPalette` `SystemCommand` callback does not receive the dismiss result.

Here is a slightly tweaked version of the QuitScreen example where it also calls the same function from the command palette. You can see that the key binding still quits the app as normal. If you do it from the command palette it does not quit. Does not matter if it is Modal or not.

```from typing import Iterable
from textual.app import App, ComposeResult, SystemCommand
from textual.containers import Grid
from textual.screen import ModalScreen, Screen
from textual.widgets import Button, Footer, Header, Label

class QuitScreen(ModalScreen[bool]):  
    """Screen with a dialog to quit."""

    def compose(self) -> ComposeResult:
        yield Grid(
            Label("Are you sure you want to quit?", id="question"),
            Button("Quit", variant="error", id="quit"),
            Button("Cancel", variant="primary", id="cancel"),
            id="dialog",
        )

    def on_button_pressed(self, event: Button.Pressed) -> None:
        if event.button.id == "quit":
            self.dismiss(True)
        else:
            self.dismiss(False)


class ModalApp(App):
    """An app with a modal dialog."""

    # CSS_PATH = "modal01.tcss"
    BINDINGS = [("q", "request_quit", "Quit")]

    def compose(self) -> ComposeResult:
        yield Header()
        yield Footer()

    def get_system_commands(self, screen: Screen) -> Iterable[SystemCommand]:
        yield from super().get_system_commands(screen)
        yield SystemCommand("try a modal quit dialog", "this should work", self.action_request_quit)

    def action_request_quit(self) -> None:
        """Action to display the quit dialog."""

        def check_quit(quit: bool | None) -> None:
            """Called when QuitScreen is dismissed."""
            if quit:
                self.exit()

        self.push_screen(QuitScreen(), check_quit)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app = ModalApp()
    app.run()
```

title: How to detect the selected node from a tree.
body:
In the attached App, pressing the button will indicate the highlighted and the selected node from the tree. In order to accomplish this, I needed to fetch the highlighted and selected event, and store the specific nodes in self.SEL_node and self.HIGH_node.
Isn't there an easier way to use an attribute from the tree variable itself?  It removes the need for storing into instance variables.

```
from textual.app import App
from textual.widgets import Tree, Button, Log
from textual.message import Message


class MyApp(App):
    def compose(self):
        self.tree_panel = Tree("Root",id="boom")
        # Create the log panel
        self.log_panel = Log()

        # Create the start and stop buttons
        self.start_button = Button("Start", id="start_button")
        yield self.tree_panel
        yield self.log_panel
        yield self.start_button

    def on_tree_node_highlighted( self, event: Tree.NodeHighlighted ) -> None:
        """Called when the user click a file in the directory tree."""
        event.stop()
        nd = event.node
        self.HIGH_node = nd
        self.log_panel.write(f"Node highlighted  {nd.label}\n")

    def on_tree_node_selected( self, event: Tree.NodeSelected ) -> None:
        """Called when the user click a file in the directory tree."""
        event.stop()
        nd = event.node
        self.SEL_node = nd
        self.log_panel.write(f"Node selected  {nd.label}\n")

    def on_mount(self):
        # Populate the tree
        tree= self.tree_panel
        node = tree.root
        node = node.add("AAA")
        node = node.add("BBB"   )

    async def on_button_pressed(self, message: Message):
        button_id = message.control.id
        high_node = self.HIGH_node    
        if high_node:
                self.log_panel.write(f"Start action highlighted for {high_node.label}\n")
        selected_node = self.SEL_node    
        if selected_node:
                self.log_panel.write(f"Start action selected for {selected_node.label}\n")

app = MyApp()
app.run()


```

title: Regression: mouse support broken in Visual Studio Code terminal
body:
Mouse support is broken in the VS Code terminal. When you click on a widget, that widget is not focused. Worse, if it _was_ focused using keyboard shortcuts, it will be blurred. It turns out that the mouse coordinates are incorrectly calculated and that if you move your mouse over the top-left corner of the terminal, the reported mouse coordinates cover the entire area. So the exact top-left is reported as (0.0, 0.0, but if you move a bit to the right and a bit down it already reports (17.0, 12.0) and so on.

I ran a git bisect and the offending commit is (unsurprisingly) 9f18dfe (smooth scrolling). I tested using this code:
```python
from textual import on
from textual.app import App, ComposeResult
from textual.events import MouseMove
from textual.widgets import RichLog


class MouseMoveApp(App[None]):
    def compose(self) -> ComposeResult:
        yield RichLog(markup=True)

    @on(MouseMove)
    def record_mouse_position(self, event: MouseMove) -> None:
        self.query_one(RichLog).write(event)


MouseMoveApp().run()
```
